name: Broken Access Control
description: Access control enforces policy such that users cannot act outside of their intended permissions. Failures typically lead to unauthorized information disclosure, modification, or destruction of all data or performing a business function outside the user's limits.
prevalence: 94% of applications tested had some form of broken access control
impact: Attackers can access unauthorized functionality and data, view other users' accounts, modify access rights
prevention: Deny by default except for public resources
Implement access control mechanisms once and re-use throughout the application
Model access controls should enforce record ownership
Disable web server directory listing
Log access control failures, alert admins

name: Cryptographic Failures
description: Formerly Sensitive Data Exposure. Focuses on failures related to cryptography which often lead to exposure of sensitive data. Includes use of weak algorithms, insufficient key lengths, poor key management, and transmission of data in clear text.
prevalence: Failures frequently result in exposure of PII, health records, credentials, business secrets
impact: Exposure of sensitive data through weak crypto, leading to compliance violations and data breaches
prevention: Classify data processed, stored, or transmitted
Don't store sensitive data unnecessarily
Encrypt all sensitive data at rest
Use strong standard algorithms and proper key management
Disable caching for sensitive responses

name: Injection
description: An application is vulnerable when user-supplied data is not validated, filtered, or sanitized, hostile data is used within dynamic queries or commands, or object-relational mapping parameters are used without sanitization.
prevalence: 94% of applications were tested for some form of injection with max incidence rate of 19%
impact: Data loss, corruption, disclosure to unauthorized parties, denial of access, complete host takeover
prevention: Use parameterized queries/prepared statements
Use positive server-side input validation
Escape special characters for residual dynamic queries
Use LIMIT and other SQL controls to prevent mass disclosure

name: Insecure Design
description: A new category for 2021, focusing on risks related to design and architectural flaws. Insecure design cannot be fixed by a perfect implementation as the necessary security controls were never created to defend against specific attacks.
prevalence: Represents a broad category requiring threat modeling, secure design patterns, and reference architectures
impact: Business logic flaws, missing security controls, inadequate threat modeling leading to exploitable weaknesses
prevention: Establish secure development lifecycle
Use threat modeling for critical authentication, access control, business logic
Integrate security language and controls into user stories
Write unit and integration tests to validate critical flows are resistant to threat model

name: Security Misconfiguration
description: The application might be vulnerable if it is missing appropriate security hardening, has improperly configured permissions on cloud services, has unnecessary features enabled, uses default accounts and passwords, or error handling reveals stack traces.
prevalence: 90% of applications tested for misconfiguration with average incidence rate of 4.5%
impact: Unauthorized access to system data or functionality, occasionally complete system compromise
prevention: Repeatable hardening process for fast, locked-down environments
Minimal platform without unnecessary features
Review and update configurations as part of patch management
Segmented application architecture
Automated process to verify effectiveness of configurations

name: Vulnerable and Outdated Components
description: Components run with same privileges as the application. If a vulnerable component is exploited, it can cause serious data loss or server takeover. Applications using known vulnerable components undermine defenses.
prevalence: Average CVE per component in most applications; known vulnerable components are extremely common
impact: Can range from minimal to complete machine compromise and data exfiltration
prevention: Remove unused dependencies and features
Continuously inventory component versions
Monitor CVE databases for vulnerabilities
Obtain components from official sources over secure links
Monitor for unmaintained libraries

name: Identification and Authentication Failures
description: Confirmation of the user's identity, authentication, and session management is critical. Authentication weaknesses include permitting brute force attacks, weak passwords, improper session handling, and credential stuffing.
prevalence: Standardized frameworks have helped but issues persist especially around token management and MFA
impact: Attackers gain access to user accounts, admin systems, and the ability to assume other users' identities
prevention: Implement multi-factor authentication
Don't ship with default credentials
Implement weak-password checks
Harden credential recovery paths
Limit or delay failed login attempts
Use server-side session manager with high-entropy session ID

name: Software and Data Integrity Failures
description: Relates to code and infrastructure that does not protect against integrity violations. Examples include auto-update without integrity verification, insecure CI/CD pipelines, and insecure deserialization.
prevalence: New category including insecure deserialization from 2017 and supply chain attacks
impact: Supply chain compromise, remote code execution via deserialization, CI/CD pipeline manipulation
prevention: Use digital signatures to verify software/data from expected source
Ensure libraries consume trusted repositories
Use software supply chain security tools
Ensure CI/CD pipeline has proper segregation, configuration, and access control
Don't send unsigned/unencrypted serialized data to untrusted clients

name: Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
description: Without logging and monitoring, breaches cannot be detected. Insufficient logging, detection, monitoring, and active response occurs any time auditable events are not logged or alerts are not triggered.
prevalence: This category is included to help detect, escalate, and respond to active breaches
impact: Inability to detect attacks and breaches, enabling attackers to persist, pivot, and extract/destroy data
prevention: Ensure login failures, access control failures, and server-side input validation failures are logged
Ensure logs are in a format easily consumed by log management solutions
Ensure high-value transactions have an audit trail
Establish effective monitoring and alerting for suspicious activities

name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
description: SSRF flaws occur whenever a web application fetches a remote resource without validating the user-supplied URL. It allows an attacker to coerce the application to send a crafted request to an unexpected destination.
prevalence: New category added due to industry survey data showing increasing SSRF attacks especially in cloud environments
impact: Access internal services behind firewalls, cloud metadata services, internal port scanning, remote code execution
prevention: Segment remote resource access from network layer
Enforce 'deny by default' firewall policies
Sanitize and validate all client-supplied input data
Disable HTTP redirections
Don't deploy other security services on front systems
